mainTopic: Saving a friend's more valuable property at the cost of your own (wine vs. honey, cheap donkey vs. expensive donkey), and why the rescuer can't simply claim the friend's goods as הפקר.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה. Someone gives up his own cheaper item, like wine or a donkey, to save his friend's more valuable one. He gets only a wage, unless he first set terms to be paid for his loss. The גמרא asks why he can't just claim the friend's goods as הפקר, since goods about to be lost seem to be ownerless. It answers with רבי ירמיה's case of a barrel wrapped in a press-basket, which was never fully lost. A chain of questions follows about making goods that are about to be lost into תרומה or מעשר: a traveler facing a robber, and ten barrels of impure wine where one broke or was left uncovered. The uncovered barrel is explained through straining the wine gently, following רבי נחמיה, and the case is set as דמאי so it fits his view on separating impure for impure. Next the גמרא asks why oil counts as a loss to the כהן but wine does not. The answer is that the wine is new, and keeping it to age risks a mishap (תקלה), while oil can be stored safely in a foul container. The amud ends by noting that the mishap worry is itself a dispute between תנאים, and the ברייתא showing this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Wine poured out to save honey: wage only, unless he set terms
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה's wine-and-honey case. The rescuer gets only his wage, but if he made a deal first, he is paid for his wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gets only his wage. But if he said, 'I will save yours, and you pay me the value of mine,' the other must pay him.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a משנה. Someone spilled his own wine to save his friend's more valuable honey, and the משנה tells us what he can collect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a deal, the rescuer is treated like a worker and gets only payment for his effort, not for the wine he lost. If he states terms before acting, the honey owner must pay for the wine. A clear agreement made in advance changes the result.

keyTerms.meaning: his wage, payment for his effort
I will save / rescue
the value of mine
he is obligated to give him

phrases.english: He has only his wage.
phrases.notes: The start of this case, pouring out wine to save a friend's honey, is on the previous page.

phrases.english: But if he said: "I will save yours,
and you will give me the value of mine",
he is obligated to give it to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rescuer who sacrificed his own goods gets only his wage, unless he set terms beforehand to be paid for his loss.

steps.title: The donkey case: same rule
steps.stepSummary: A river sweeps away two donkeys. The owner of the cheaper one saves the more expensive one. He gets only his wage, unless he made a deal first.
steps.simpleTranslation: A river swept away his donkey (worth 100) and his friend's donkey (worth 200). He let his own go and saved his friend's, so he gets only his wage. If he first said, 'I'll save yours and you give me mine,' the friend must pay him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second example with the same rule, this time with two donkeys in a river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too, giving up your own property to save someone else's gets you only a wage. Only an agreement made beforehand earns you the value of what you lost. The second example shows the rule is general and not special to wine and honey.

keyTerms.meaning: a river swept away
a coin worth 100 dinars
and he left (abandoned)

steps.whatToRemember: In both משנה cases, a rescuer who gives up his own item gets only a wage, unless he set terms before acting.

phrases.english: A river swept away his donkey and his friend's donkey,
his was worth a מנה (100 dinars)
and his friend's was worth two hundred,
and this one left his own
and saved his friend's,
he has only his wage.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ: ״אֲנִי אַצִּיל אֶת שֶׁלְּךָ,
phrases.english: But if he said to him: "I will save yours,
and you will give me mine",
he is obligated to give it to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case with the same ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saving a friend's more valuable donkey instead of your own earns only a wage, unless you made terms beforehand.

steps.title: Why can't he claim the honey as ownerless?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the rescuer gets only a wage. Why can't he say the honey was ownerless and he acquired it himself?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let him say to the owner: 'I am acquiring it from ownerless property!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by challenging the משנה. If the honey was about to be lost, it seems to be הפקר, so whoever saves it should own it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that property about to be destroyed is given up by its owner and becomes הפקר. If so, the rescuer should keep the whole honey, not just collect a wage. This makes the משנה's 'only his wage' rule look wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
and why?
ownerless property, which anyone may take
I am acquiring

phrases.english: GEMARA: But why?
Let him say to him:
"I am acquiring from ownerless property!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the rescuer gets only his wage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Goods about to be lost are הפקר, so the rescuer should acquire them outright.

steps.title: Proof that goods about to be lost are ownerless
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone whose jugs are breaking cannot declare their contents תרומה and מעשר for other produce. This shows such goods no longer count as his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it taught: someone carrying jugs of wine and oil who saw them breaking should not say, 'This is תרומה and מעשר for produce in my house,' and if he did say it, his words mean nothing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its question with a ברייתא showing that goods about to be lost are treated as ownerless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only separate תרומה and מעשר from something that belongs to you. Since his declaration on the breaking jugs does nothing, the contents must already count as הפקר. If so, the rescued honey should also be הפקר.

keyTerms.meaning: isn't it taught (in a ברייתא)?
breaking
the gifts separated from produce for the כהן and לוי
he has said nothing, his words have no effect

phrases.english: Isn't it taught:
One who was carrying
jugs of wine and jugs of oil,
and saw that they were breaking,
should not say: "This is hereby תרומה and tithe

phrases.aramaic: עַל פֵּירוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתִי״,
phrases.english: for produce that I have in my house",
and if he said it, he has said nothing?
phrases.notes: His words do nothing because the leaking contents no longer count as his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the question in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Goods about to be lost are considered הפקר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a declaration of תרומה on breaking jugs has no effect.

steps.title: The honey barrel was wrapped in a press-basket
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי ירמיה, the גמרא answers that the honey barrel had a press-basket wrapped around it. It was not fully lost, so it never became הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי ירמיה said: when the basket of the olive press is wrapped around it. So too here, when the basket of the olive press is wrapped around it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by limiting the משנה to a case where the honey barrel had a basket wrapped around it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the basket around it, the barrel would not break completely and some honey would stay inside. Goods that are not fully lost do not become הפקר, so the owner still owns the honey. The rescuer therefore cannot claim it and gets only his wage.

keyTerms.meaning: the basket used in the olive press
wrapped around it
so too (here)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rescuer gets only a wage because the honey was not fully lost (the barrel was wrapped), so it never became הפקר.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not reject the idea that fully lost goods are הפקר. It only says that in our משנה's case the honey was not fully lost.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yirmeya said:
when the basket of the olive press is wrapped around it;
phrases.notes: The basket keeps the barrel from breaking completely, so some of what is inside stays.

phrases.english: so too here,
it is when the basket of the olive press is wrapped around it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 3–4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the משנה refers to a barrel wrapped in a press-basket.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The honey was about to be lost completely, so it was הפקר and the rescuer could claim it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel was protected, so it was not fully lost. The owner keeps ownership, and the rescuer gets only his wage.

steps.title: A traveler facing a robber: his declaration does work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling that declaring breaking jugs as holy 'said nothing.' Another ברייתא says a traveler who transfers his מעשר שני onto money threatened by a robber has a valid declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that if he said it, he said nothing? But a ברייתא teaches: someone traveling with money in his hand sees a robber coming toward him. He should not say, 'The produce in my house is hereby redeemed onto these coins.' But if he did say it, his words stand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last line of the earlier ברייתא, which said that declaring breaking jugs as תרומה and מעשר 'said nothing.' It brings a different ברייתא where a declaration over money that is about to be lost does take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases a person gives a holy status to something he is about to lose. Yet the robber ברייתא says the declaration works בדיעבד, while the jugs ברייתא says it is worthless. These two rulings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A robber or violent person
Redeemed, meaning the holiness of מעשר שני produce moves onto money
Coins, money
His words stand, meaning the declaration takes effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ברייתות. The jugs ברייתא says the declaration does nothing. The robber ברייתא says you should not do it, but if you do, it works.

phrases.english: And if he said it, he has said nothing?
phrases.notes: This quotes the end of the jugs ברייתא from step 4.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
One who was traveling on the road
with money in his hand
and a robber coming toward him,
should not say:
'The produce that I have in my house
is hereby redeemed onto these coins,'
phrases.notes: The produce is מעשר שני. Its holiness would move onto the coins, which the robber is about to take.

phrases.english: but if he did say it, his words stand!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר – לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the closing ruling of the ברייתא brought in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that declaring breaking jugs as תרומה and מעשר is worthless.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel case, money about to be lost to a robber, shows that such a declaration does take effect after the fact.

steps.title: The traveler could still save his money
steps.stepSummary: The robber case is one where the traveler is able to save his money, so it is not truly lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where he is able to save his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In the robber case the money is not really lost, because the traveler can still save it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The breaking jugs are truly lost, so declaring them holy means nothing. The traveler's money can still be rescued, so it still counts as his and the declaration works. The two ברייתות describe different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows the case)
Able to save or rescue

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where he is able to save it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by narrowing the robber case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The robber ברייתא seemed to describe money that is surely lost, just like the breaking jugs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The traveler can still rescue his money, so it is not lost and the declaration works.

steps.title: If he can save it, why not do it from the start?
steps.stepSummary: If the money can be saved, why does the ברייתא say he should not make the declaration לכתחילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is able to save it, why should he not say it from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the money is safe enough, the ברייתא should let him redeem the produce even לכתחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'he should not say' it, which suggests some real danger. But if he can save the money, there seems to be no danger at all. So the answer seems to explain too much.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, the ideal way to act (as opposed to בדיעבד, after the fact)
Why?

phrases.english: If it is where he is able to save it,
why should he not say it from the start?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּשֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַצִּיל, לְכַתְּחִלָּה אַמַּאי לֹא יֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the traveler is able to save his money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the money is safe, the ברייתא's ban on declaring לכתחילה has no reason.

steps.title: He can save it, but only with difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The traveler can save the money only with great effort, so ideally he should not risk it, but after the fact the declaration works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he is able to save it only with difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא refines its answer. The traveler can save the money, but only with great effort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since saving the money is hard, the holy coins really might be lost, so he should not redeem onto them לכתחילה. Since saving is still possible, the money is not counted as lost, so בדיעבד the declaration takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: With difficulty, under pressure

steps.whatToRemember: The robber case is a middle level of loss: the money can be saved with difficulty. So the rule is: do not do it לכתחילה, but בדיעבד it works.

phrases.english: Where he is able to save it, but only with difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by making the case narrower.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Able to save' sounded like there is no risk, so there was no reason to forbid it לכתחילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Saving is possible but hard, so it is not ideal, yet it still works after the fact.

steps.title: Ten barrels: declaring a breaking barrel is allowed
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא lets a person ideally declare a broken or uncovered barrel of impure wine as תרומת מעשר, even though there is a loss. Only with oil is it forbidden, because of the כהן's loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that wherever there is a loss, one should not say it from the start? But a ברייתא teaches: someone had ten barrels of impure טבל, and he saw that one of them broke or was left uncovered. He may say, 'This is hereby תרומת מעשר for the other nine.' But with oil he should not do this, because of the loss to the כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 9 that any risk of loss means you should not make the declaration לכתחילה. It brings a ברייתא where a person may declare a barrel that is being lost, even from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 suggested that when something might be lost, you should not give it a holy status לכתחילה. But in the ten-barrels case the man ideally declares a breaking barrel as תרומת מעשר. The ברייתא only forbids this with oil, because of the כהן's loss, which implies that with wine he is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure produce from which the required gifts have not yet been taken
The tenth of the מעשר that is given to a כהן
It was left uncovered
A loss to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Here the ברייתא allows it even לכתחילה, which is a stronger ruling than the robber case, where it only works בדיעבד.

phrases.english: And wherever there is a loss,
should he not say it from the start?
But isn't it taught:
If one had
ten barrels of impure untithed produce,
phrases.notes: From the rest of the ברייתא we see these are barrels of wine, since oil is mentioned as a separate case.

phrases.english: and he saw that one of them
had broken or had been left uncovered,
he may say:
'This is hereby the תרומת מעשר
for its nine companions.'
But with oil he should not do so,
because of the כהן's loss!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא הֶפְסֵידָא, לְכַתְּחִלָּה לֹא יֹאמַר? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle behind the answer in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that wherever there is a risk of loss, one should not make the declaration לכתחילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ten-barrels ברייתא lets a person declare a barrel that is being lost even לכתחילה, as long as it is wine and not oil.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: a press-basket was wrapped around the barrel
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that in the ten-barrels case a press-basket was wrapped around the barrel, so the wine stays inside and is not truly lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is when the basket of the olive press was wrapped around it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge. The broken barrel had a press-basket wrapped around it, so its wine did not spill out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the basket holding the wine in, there is no real loss. That is why the person may declare it לכתחילה. So the ten-barrels case does not prove that you may ideally declare something that is actually being lost.

keyTerms.meaning: The basket of the olive press
Wrapped around it

phrases.english: רבי ירמיה said:
When the basket of the olive press
is wrapped around it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: כְּשֶׁעֵקֶל בֵּית הַבַּד כָּרוּךְ עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by narrowing the ten-barrels case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The broken barrel seemed to be truly losing its wine, yet he could still declare it לכתחילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The basket kept the wine inside, so nothing was really lost.

steps.title: The basket helps a broken barrel, but what about an uncovered one?
steps.stepSummary: The basket answer works for a broken barrel, but an uncovered barrel is a problem for a different reason, so what use is its wine?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a barrel that broke: the wine is still usable. But a barrel that was left uncovered, what is it good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה's answer. A basket keeps wine from leaking, but it does nothing for a barrel that was left uncovered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke of two cases: a broken barrel and an uncovered one. The basket explains why the broken barrel's wine is not lost. But uncovered wine is not usable, so the declaration still seems to be made over something worthless, and the challenge comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for this case (the first half of a challenge)
It is fit, usable

phrases.english: It makes sense for one that broke: it is still usable,
but one that was uncovered, what is it fit for?
phrases.notes: Uncovered drinks were forbidden for drinking, so the basket does not help this barrel at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה – חַזְיָא, אֶלָּא נִתְגַּלְּתָה – לְמַאי חַזְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ירמיה's answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's answer that a press-basket kept the barrel's wine from being lost.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer only covers a broken barrel. It does not explain the uncovered barrel, whose wine cannot be used.

steps.title: Uncovered wine cannot even be used for sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the uncovered wine might still be used for sprinkling. It knocks this down with a ברייתא that forbids every use of uncovered water, including sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the uncovered wine is still good for sprinkling, a ברייתא teaches otherwise: water that was left uncovered may not be poured out in a public place, may not be used to knead clay, may not be sprinkled on a house floor, and may not be given to one's own animal or a friend's animal to drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible use for the uncovered wine (sprinkling it) and then shoots that idea down right away. This strengthens the question from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wine were good for sprinkling, it would not be a total loss. But the ברייתא lists sprinkling a house floor among the forbidden uses of uncovered liquid. So sprinkling cannot be the use, and the question from step 12 stands even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a possible answer that is about to be rejected
Sprinkling a liquid around, for example to give off a nice smell
Leaving a liquid uncovered, where a snake may have drunk from it and left venom
To sprinkle water on a floor to settle the dust
To knead or mix (clay)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא talks about water, while our case is wine. The גמרא is using the water rule to show that uncovered liquids in general cannot be used for sprinkling.

phrases.english: And if you would say it is fit for sprinkling,
phrases.notes: "It" is the wine from the uncovered barrel in step 12.

phrases.english: but isn't it taught: water that was left uncovered —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִשְׁפְּכֵם בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים;
phrases.english: one may not pour it out in the public domain;
nor knead clay with it;
nor sprinkle the house with it;
nor give his animal to drink from it,
nor his friend's animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible way out of the question in step 12, making that question stronger.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that uncovered wine still has a use (sprinkling), so declaring it causes no loss.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids every use of uncovered liquid, sprinkling included, so the wine really is worthless.

steps.title: The wine can be passed through a strainer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the uncovered wine is usable if it is poured through a strainer, following the view of רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he passed the wine through a strainer, following רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the uncovered barrel: strain the wine, and it can be used. The next step brings the source for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If straining removes the danger, the uncovered wine is not lost, and declaring it תרומת מעשר is no loss to the כהן. The answer depends on רבי נחמיה's opinion, which is quoted next.

keyTerms.meaning: A strainer or filter
That he passed it (through)

phrases.english: It is where he passed it through a strainer,
in line with רבי נחמיה —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from steps 12-13 by showing how the uncovered wine can still be used.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical fix: straining the wine makes it usable.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Uncovered wine has no use at all, so declaring it is a loss to the כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine that is strained, following רבי נחמיה, is usable, so the declaration causes no real loss.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: venom floats like a sponge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא with רבי נחמיה's view. If the lower vessel under the strainer is covered, the liquid is fine, because venom floats and stays on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: a strainer is subject to the rule of uncovering. רבי נחמיה said: When is that? When the lower vessel is uncovered. But when the lower vessel is covered, even if the upper one is uncovered, there is no problem of uncovering, because snake venom is like a sponge: it floats and stays in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the strainer answer. רבי נחמיה explains why straining protects the liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says a strainer does not help. רבי נחמיה says it does, as long as the lower vessel that catches the strained liquid is covered. The reason is that venom floats on top like a sponge and stays in the strainer instead of passing down.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower vessel that catches the liquid after it goes through the strainer
The upper vessel, where the strainer sits
Venom
A sponge
Floats

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a strainer works: the venom stays on top and does not pass through. That idea is exactly what the next challenge questions.

phrases.english: As it is taught: a strainer
is subject to the rule of uncovering.
רבי נחמיה said: When is this so?
When the lower vessel is uncovered,
but when the lower vessel is covered —
even though the upper one is uncovered,
it is not subject to the rule of uncovering;

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֶרֶס שֶׁל נָחָשׁ דּוֹמֶה לִסְפוֹג,
phrases.english: because a snake's venom is like a sponge,
and it floats and stays in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מְסַנֶּנֶת, יֵשׁ בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and the reasoning behind the strainer answer in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That straining makes uncovered liquid usable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי נחמיה: venom floats like a sponge and stays in the strainer.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה only holds if the wine was not shaken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the strainer answer. רבי יהושע בן לוי said רבי נחמיה's rule works only if the liquid was not shaken up, and pouring a barrel out shakes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about this: רבי סימון said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: They only taught this when he did not shake it up, but if he shook it up, it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the strainer answer by quoting a limit on רבי נחמיה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה's reason is that the venom floats on top. Once the liquid is shaken up, the venom mixes in and can pass through the strainer. Pouring wine out of a barrel would naturally shake it, so straining should not help here.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it said about this? (introduces a statement that limits a source)
They only taught this when...: a phrase that narrows a rule
He shook it up or stirred it

phrases.english: Wasn't it said about it,
phrases.notes: "It" is רבי נחמיה's ruling from the last step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי סִימוֹן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: רבי סימון said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי:
They only taught this where he did not shake it up,
but if he shook it up, it is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי סִימוֹן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the strainer answer by limiting the source it depends on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 14 that straining makes the barrel's wine usable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נחמיה's rule works only for liquid that was not shaken. Wine poured out of a barrel gets shaken, so the venom could pass through the strainer.

steps.title: Drain the barrel gently so it is not shaken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that here too, one can put something on the mouth of the barrel so the wine drips out slowly, without shaking it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is possible to place something on the mouth of the barrel, and it drains the wine out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the strainer answer by showing how to get the wine out without shaking it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that pouring would shake up the wine and mix in the venom. If something is placed on the mouth of the barrel and the wine is drained through it slowly, the wine is never shaken. So רבי נחמיה's rule still applies, the wine is usable, and the declaration causes no loss.

keyTerms.meaning: There too: the same fix works in this case
It is possible
On the mouth of the barrel
Drains out or filters the liquid gently

steps.whatToRemember: The uncovered barrel is not a total loss: if the wine is drained out gently through a strainer without being shaken, it can be used (following רבי נחמיה). That is why declaring it תרומת מעשר is allowed.

phrases.english: There too,
phrases.notes: "There" is the uncovered barrel case from the ברייתא in step 10.

phrases.english: it is possible to place something on the mouth of the barrel,
and it drains it out gently.
phrases.notes: The standard גמרא says דְּשָׁפֵי; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is וְשָׁפֵי. The meaning is the same either way.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, אֶפְשָׁר דְּמַנַּח מִידֵּי אַפּוּמָּא דְחָבִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by showing the wine can be taken out without being shaken.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical method: drain the wine gently so the shaking problem never comes up.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Getting wine out of a barrel always shakes it, so the strainer would not help.
steps.terutzMaskana: Placing something on the barrel's mouth lets the wine drain slowly without being shaken, so רבי נחמיה's rule applies.

steps.title: Does רבי נחמיה allow separating from impure for impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation that follows רבי נחמיה. A ברייתא shows that רבי נחמיה allows separating impure for impure only for דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי נחמיה let us separate תרומה from impure produce for impure produce? A ברייתא teaches: you may separate from impure for impure, from pure for pure, and from pure for impure, but not from impure for pure. רבי נחמיה says: even impure for impure was allowed only for דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא was just explained according to רבי נחמיה. Now the גמרא asks how that can work, since רבי נחמיה seems stricter about separating impure for impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא lets a person name impure wine as תרומה for other impure wine. Another ברייתא shows that רבי נחמיה allows impure-for-impure only for דמאי. So the challenge is that our ברייתא cannot simply follow רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: We separate תרומה, the part of the produce given to the כהן
Ritually impure
Ritually pure
Produce bought from someone who may not have tithed it, so it is tithed only out of doubt

steps.confusionAlert: רבי נחמיה is not saying impure-for-impure is always fine. He is saying it is allowed only for דמאי. That limit is exactly what causes the problem.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Nechemya, (from impure for impure) do we separate teruma?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Either way, the question is about separating from impure produce for impure produce.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: תּוֹרְמִין מִן הַטָּמֵא עַל הַטָּמֵא,
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: One may separate teruma from the impure for the impure,
and from the pure for the pure,
and from the pure for the impure;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא מִן הַטָּמֵא עַל הַטָּהוֹר.
phrases.english: but not from the impure for the pure.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: אַף מִן הַטָּמֵא עַל הַטָּמֵא
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says: Even from the impure for the impure,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִתִּירוּ לִתְרוֹם, אֶלָּא בְּשֶׁל דְּמַאי!
phrases.english: they permitted separating teruma only for demai!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the strainer answer that follows רבי נחמיה holds up, the גמרא checks whether רבי נחמיה would agree with the rest of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה, even though it allows naming impure wine as תרומה for impure wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נחמיה allows impure-for-impure only for דמאי, but the ברייתא allows it with no limit.

steps.title: The case is דמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our ברייתא is also talking about דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the case is דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the wine in our ברייתא is דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה allows impure-for-impure for דמאי. If our ברייתא is about דמאי wine, it fits his view with no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too

phrases.english: Here too, it is dealing with demai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about ordinary טבל, which רבי נחמיה would not allow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about דמאי, where רבי נחמיה does allow impure-for-impure.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא's rule about oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the last line of the ten-barrels ברייתא from step 10: oil should not be handled this way, because the כהן would lose out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: With oil he should not do this, because of the כהן's loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last line of the ten-barrels ברייתא (step 10) to set up a new question. Oil from a breaking barrel may not be named as תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With wine, the owner may name the spilling wine as תרומה. With oil he may not, because the כהן would be harmed. The next step asks why oil and wine are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A loss to the כהן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: וּבְשֶׁמֶן לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה כֵּן,
phrases.english: The Master said: But with oil he should not do so,
phrases.notes: "Do so" means name the liquid spilling from the breaking barrel as תרומה for other barrels.

phrases.english: because of the priest's loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the closing clause of the ten-barrels ברייתא from step 10 (the oil exception) to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A breaking barrel of impure oil may not be named as תרומה, because the כהן would lose out.

steps.title: Wine can be used too, for sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why oil is different. If the reason is that oil can be burned, then wine can also be used, by sprinkling it for its smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes oil different? That it can be used for lighting? Wine can also be used, for sprinkling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why only oil counts as a loss to the כהן. Wine also has a use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure תרומה oil is still worth something to the כהן, because he can burn it for light. But impure wine is also worth something, because it can be sprinkled to give off a nice smell. So the wine case should also count as a loss to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
To light, to burn for light
Sprinkling wine to give off a pleasant smell

phrases.english: What is different about oil? That it is fit for lighting?
Wine is also fit for sprinkling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the difference the ברייתא makes between oil and wine, which was quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that only oil, and not wine, causes a loss to the כהן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both liquids still have a use for the כהן even when impure: oil for light, wine for sprinkling. So both should count as a loss.

steps.title: Sprinkling is valuable, as שמואל taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the reply that sprinkling is unimportant. It quotes שמואל in the name of רבי חייא: wine for sprinkling is worth twice as much as wine for drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say sprinkling is nothing, didn't שמואל say in the name of רבי חייא: people drink from a לוג worth a סלע, and they sprinkle from a לוג worth two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its challenge. It shows that sprinkling wine is an important use, not a small one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might answer that sprinkling is too small a use to count. שמואל's teaching shows that wine good enough for sprinkling costs twice as much as drinking wine. So the wine really is valuable to the כהן, and the challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (heading off a possible answer)
It is nothing, it is unimportant
A measure of liquid
A coin of fairly high value

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא זִילּוּף לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא,
phrases.english: And if you would say sprinkling is nothing,
but didn't Shmuel say in the name of Rabbi Chiya:
One drinks from a log worth a sela,
and one sprinkles from a log worth two!
phrases.notes: "Two" means two סלעים. The wine people use for sprinkling is the more expensive kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא זִילּוּף לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא, וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the challenge in step 21 by blocking an easy way out.
steps.raayaObject: That sprinkling wine is an important use, so the כהן would lose out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל in the name of רבי חייא: sprinkling wine is worth two סלעים a לוג, and drinking wine only one.

steps.title: The case is new wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about new wine, which is not yet fit for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with new wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wine in the ברייתא is new wine, so it cannot be used for sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New wine does not yet have a strong smell, so sprinkling it does nothing. That means the כהן loses nothing with this wine, unlike oil, which can always be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrowed case)
New wine that has not aged yet

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with new wine.
phrases.notes: New wine has not developed its smell yet, so it is no good for sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 21 and 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any wine can be sprinkled, so the כהן would lose out with wine just as with oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about new wine, which is not fit for sprinkling, so there is no loss.

steps.title: But the new wine can be aged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the new wine could be left to age, and then it would be good for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it fit to be aged?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new-wine answer. The כהן could just wait for the wine to age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if new wine is useless right now, it becomes good for sprinkling with time. So the כהן would still lose something.

keyTerms.meaning: To age it, to let it get old

phrases.english: But it is fit to be aged!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that new wine has no use for sprinkling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: New wine turns into old wine over time, so it has a future use for sprinkling.

steps.title: Aging it could lead to a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that keeping impure תרומה wine around to age could lead to a mishap, so it is not counted as usable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could come to a mishap through it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that aging the wine is not allowed, because keeping it around could lead to a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If impure תרומה wine is stored for a long time, someone might forget what it is and drink it, which is forbidden. Since it may not be kept to age, new wine really has no use, and the כהן loses nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A mishap, a stumbling into doing something forbidden
He will come through it (to something)

steps.whatToRemember: Oil and wine are treated differently. Impure תרומה oil can always be burned, so the כהן would lose out. The ברייתא's wine is new wine, which cannot be sprinkled now and may not be kept to age because of the risk of a mishap. So naming it as תרומה costs the כהן nothing.

phrases.english: He will come through it to a mishap.
phrases.notes: The worry is that someone might forget this is impure תרומה and drink it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 and finishes the oil-versus-wine discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic safeguard: keeping it is not allowed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: New wine could be aged, so it has a future use and its loss would harm the כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Aging impure תרומה wine is not allowed because it could lead to a mishap, so new wine has no use and the כהן loses nothing.

steps.title: Oil should also carry the risk of a mishap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 25: if keeping impure wine could lead to a mishap, keeping impure oil should carry the same risk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Oil should also be able to lead to a mishap!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer from step 25 against itself. If the worry of a mishap means wine may not be kept, the same worry should apply to oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 the גמרא said impure תרומה wine is not counted as usable, because keeping it around might lead someone to drink it by mistake. Oil could also be eaten or drunk by mistake. So the question is why the oil may be kept.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil
A mishap; here, accidentally eating or drinking forbidden impure תרומה
Comes to; ends up in

phrases.english: Oil, too, one could come with it
to a mishap!

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמֶן נָמֵי אָתֵי בֵּיהּ לִידֵי תַּקָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 25 by applying it to oil.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 25, that the risk of a mishap makes impure wine count as unusable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consistency: the same risk exists with oil, yet oil is treated as usable.

steps.title: The oil is kept in a disgusting container
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that impure תרומה oil is stored in a foul container, so no one will mistakenly eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he places it in a disgusting container.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about oil. The oil is put into a disgusting container, so nobody will come to eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil being kept only for burning does not need to stay pleasant. Putting it in a foul container takes away the risk of a mishap. So the worry from step 25 does not apply to oil.

keyTerms.meaning: He places; he puts
A disgusting, foul container

phrases.english: Because he places it
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets. Either way, he's putting the oil away.

phrases.english: in a disgusting container.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical difference: the way the oil is stored removes the risk.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oil carries the same risk of a mishap as wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Oil is stored in a foul container, so there is no risk anyone will eat it.

steps.title: Then put the wine in a disgusting container too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the same solution should work for wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him place the wine, too, in a disgusting container!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the wine cannot be handled the same way. Put it in a foul container, and the risk is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 removed the risk for oil by storing it in a foul container. If that works for oil, it should work for wine too. Then the wine could also be kept and used for sprinkling.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine

phrases.english: Wine, too, let him place it
in a disgusting container!

steps.triggerLanguage: יַיִן נָמֵי מַנַּח לֵיהּ בִּכְלִי מָאוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 27 to challenge the difference between oil and wine.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 27, that the foul container solves the problem only for oil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the foul-container solution works for oil, it should work for wine as well.

steps.title: Wine for sprinkling would be ruined in a foul container
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that someone who wants the wine for its nice smell would never store it in a disgusting container.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if he wants it for sprinkling, would he put it in a disgusting container?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the solution does not work for wine. The whole point of keeping it is its pleasant smell, and a foul container would ruin that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil is used for burning, so a foul container does not hurt it. Wine is kept for sprinkling (זילוף) because of its smell, so it must stay in a clean container. That means the risk of a mishap stays, and wine may not be kept while oil may.

keyTerms.meaning: Now; here a way of saying "since this is the case, would he really...?"
Sprinkling, wine sprinkled for its pleasant smell
He wants it

steps.whatToRemember: Impure תרומה oil may be kept because it can be stored in a foul container for burning. Impure תרומה wine cannot be stored that way, because sprinkling needs its smell, so the risk of a mishap remains.

phrases.english: Now, if he wants it for sprinkling,
would he put it in a disgusting container?!
phrases.notes: This is a question that expects "of course not": the bad container would spoil the smell he wants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 and closes the oil-versus-wine discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: what each item is used for decides how it can be stored.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wine could be kept safely in a foul container, just like oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine kept for sprinkling must stay in a clean container, so the risk of a mishap remains.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the ruling treats impure תרומה oil and wine differently, even though both could cause a mishap.

steps.title: The worry about a mishap is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the worry about a mishap is itself argued about by תנאים, and begins quoting a ברייתא about a barrel of impure תרומה wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the worry about a mishap itself is a dispute between תנאים. As it is taught: a barrel of תרומה wine that became impure — בית שמאי say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It says the mishap worry is disputed by תנאים and starts quoting the ברייתא that shows this, ending just as בית שמאי begin to speak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא used the mishap worry as a reason everyone accepts. Now it adds that not all תנאים agree with it. The case of a barrel of impure תרומה wine will show the two sides, and their opinions come next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
A barrel
It became impure
The students of שמאי

phrases.english: And the mishap worry itself
is a dispute between תנאים –
as it is taught:
a barrel of תרומה wine
that became impure –
בית שמאי say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After using the mishap worry to settle the oil-versus-wine question, the גמרא steps back to show that the worry itself is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The worry about a mishap (תקלה) is not agreed on by everyone. It is a dispute between תנאים, shown in a ברייתא about a barrel of impure תרומה wine.
